{{Short description|American physicist (born 1964)}}
[[File:Djordje Minic.jpg|thumb|Djordje Minic]]
'''Djordje Minic''' (born 23 April 1964) is an American physicist of Yugoslav descent. His main subject of research is quantum physics. He graduated from the Faculty of Electrical Engineering in Belgrade in 1988, and received a PhD in Physics in 1993, at the [[University of Texas at Austin|University of Texas, Austin]] in the group of [[Steven Weinberg]] and [[Joseph Polchinski]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Djordje Minic |url=https://www1.phys.vt.edu/~dminic/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=www1.phys.vt.edu}}</ref>

He conducted postdoctoral research at The City College of New York, The University of Chicago, The Pennsylvania State University and at the Center for Theoretical Physics at the California Institute of Technology.<ref name=":0" />

In 2001, he relocated to Blacksburg, Virginia, where he currently resides and serves as a professor at [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University]].<ref name=":0" />

His primary research interests lie at the intersection of quantum gravity, string theory, and quantum chromodynamics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Berglund |first=Per |last2=Geraci |first2=Andrew |last3=Hübsch |first3=Tristan |last4=Mattingly |first4=David |last5=Minic |first5=Djordje |date=2023-08-03 |title=Triple interference, non-linear Talbot effect and gravitization of the quantum |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1361-6382/ace14a |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=40 |issue=15 |pages=155008 |doi=10.1088/1361-6382/ace14a |issn=0264-9381|doi-access=free |arxiv=2303.15645 }}</ref>

In collaboration with [[Robert Leigh (physicist)|Robert Leigh]] and [[Laurent Freidel]], Professor Minic co-proposed the metastring theory, which introduces a novel formulation of quantum gravity and modular spacetime.

He also actively collaborates with Tristan Hübsch, Per Berglund, David Mattingly, and Andrew Geraci.<ref name=":1" />

In recognition of his contributions to theoretical physics he has received the [[Buchalter Cosmology Prize]] (2nd place, 2018),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buchalter Prize |url=https://www.buchaltercosmologyprize.org/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=www.buchaltercosmologyprize.org}}</ref> the Marko Jaric Prize,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dodeljen „srpski Nobel“ za fiziku |url=https://www.rts.rs/lat/magazin/nauka/4300659/dodeljen-srpski-nobel-za-fiziku.html |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=РТС |language=sr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2022-04-19 |title=AWARDS: Đorđe Minić, winner of the "Marko Jaric" prize |url=https://www.ipb.ac.rs/en/news/awards-djordje-minic-winner-of-the-marko-jaric-prize/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=IPB |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-18 |title=Nagrada "Marko Jarić" za 2020. Đorđu Miniću - Društvo - Dnevni list Danas |url=https://www.danas.rs/vesti/drustvo/nagrada-marko-jaric-za-2020-djordju-minicu/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |language=sr-RS}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vojvodine |first=Javna medijska ustanova JMU Radio-televizija |title="Srpski Nobel za fiziku" Đorđu Miniću, profesoru Univerziteta Virdžinija Tek |url=https://www.rtv.rs/sr_lat/zivot/nauka-i-tehnologija/srpski-nobel-za-fiziku-djordju-minicu-profesoru-univerziteta-virdzinija-tek_1219196.html |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=JMU Radio-televizija Vojvodine |language=sr-Latn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jokić-Stamenković |first=Dragana |title=„Srpski Nobel za fiziku” dodeljen profesoru Đorđu Miniću |url=https://www.politika.rs/sr/clanak/475336/srpski-nobel-za-fiziku-dodeljen-profesoru-dordu-minicu |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=Politika Online}}</ref> also known as The Serbian Nobel Prize in Physics, and Second Prize in the 2021 Essay Competition of the Gravity Research Foundation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Freidel |first=Laurent |last2=Kowalski-Glikman |first2=Jerzy |last3=Leigh |first3=Robert G. |last4=Minic |first4=Djordje |date=2021-10-15 |title=Quantum Gravity Phenomenology in the Infrared |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/2104.00802 |journal=International Journal of Modern Physics D |volume=30 |issue=14 |pages=2141002 |doi=10.1142/S0218271821410029 |issn=0218-2718|arxiv=2104.00802 }}</ref> Additionally, he is a foreign member of the Serbian Academy of Nonlinear Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MEMBERSHIP – СРПСКА АКАДЕМИЈА НЕЛИНЕАРНИХ НАУКА |url=https://sann.rs/en/membership/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Minic authored the book “In Search of Another Miraculous Year” (published in Belgrade, Serbia, in 2005)<ref name=":0" /> and co-authored the book ‘“The Weight of Quantum: Quantum Theory and the Structure of Physics” (published on 21 July 2026) with Tristan Hübsch.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hübsch |first=Tristan |url=https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/9781003710196 |title=The Weight of Quantum: Quantum Theory and the Structure of Physics |last2=Minic |first2=Djordje |date=2026-06-04 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=978-1-003-71019-6 |edition=1 |location=Boca Raton |language=en |doi=10.1201/9781003710196}}</ref>
